entry.title: On Born-Infeld-type higher-spin interactions and supersymmetry
entry.summary: We develop a simple Lorentz-covariant construction of the Born--Infeld-type cubic interactions $(s, s_1, s_2)$ of massless higher-spin fields with $s + s_1 + s_2$ derivatives in four-dimensiona flat space. For arbitrary spins $s \ge s_1 \ge s_2$, the vertex is formulated in terms of a conserved higher-spin current and its trace. In contrast to the famous Berends--Burgers--van Dam currents, these currents are constructed from higher-spin Weyl tensors of a single chirality, schematically $J \sim \partial C \partial C$. Starting with a general ansatz, we derive recurrence relations fixing the current coefficients, identify the unique non-trivial conserved current after eliminating trivial (fake) vertices, and show that in the range $s \le s_1 + s_2$ the interaction admits a manifestly gauge-invariant representation in terms of higher-spin Weyl tensors. The construction is then extended to $\mathcal{N}=1$ and $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetry using the corresponding off-shell superfield formalisms. In the $\mathcal{N}=1$ case, we obtain the general conserved integer superspin $s$ supercurrent with manifest supersymmetry, which is bilinear in the Weyl supertensors of superspins $Y_1$ and $Y_2$. For identical superfields, $Y_1 = Y_2$, this supercurrent vanishes for odd $s$ and is in agreement with earlier results by Gates and Koutrolikos. In the $\mathcal{N}=2$ case, using harmonic superspace, we construct the principal higher-spin supercurrent whose coefficients are uniquely fixed by the conservation equations. In contrast to the $\mathcal{N}=0,1$ cases, for identical $\mathcal{N}=2$ superfields, the corresponding vertex does not vanish. The results provide a systematic framework for Born--Infeld-type higher-spin interactions and their supersymmetric extensions.

entry.title: Breathing and quadrupole modes in squeezed Bose-Bose liquid drops
entry.summary: We investigate the lowest excitation modes of binary $^{39}$K ultradilute droplets confined harmonically in one direction, which reduces the critical number of particles needed to sustain a self-bound state. Using the density functional built from first-principles quantum Monte Carlo calculations (QMC), which incorporates the effects of finite range interactions, we study the crossover of the oscillation modes from three to two dimensions. For weak squeezing, we observe the coupling between breathing and quadrupole modes, resulting from the breaking of spherical symmetry. Increasing the squeezing, the higher-frequency mode corresponding to three-dimensional breathing mode becomes unstable. For squeezings stronger and comparable to experiments, we analyze the dependence of the excitation modes on the droplet size for several interactions and show the reduction of the number of particles needed to sustain stable oscillations. The differences between the results obtained with the QMC functional and the extended Gross-Pitaevskii theory are increased with respect to the case of previously studied spherical droplets.

entry.title: The symplectic isotopy problem for rational cuspidal curves
entry.summary: We define a suitably tame class of singular symplectic curves in 4-manifolds, namely those whose singularities are modeled on complex curve singularities. We study the corresponding symplectic isotopy problem, with a focus on rational curves with irreducible singularities (rational cuspidal curves) in the complex projective plane. We prove that every such curve is isotopic to a complex curve in degrees up to 5, and for curves with one singularity whose link is a torus knot. Classification results of symplectic isotopy classes rely on pseudo-holomorphic curves together with a symplectic version of birational geometry of log pairs and techniques from 4-dimensional topology.

entry.title: The Penrose Correspondence over a Non-Archimedean Field
entry.summary: Let $K$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and let $V$ be a four-dimensional symplectic $K$-vector space. We study the Penrose incidence correspondence $\mathbb{P}(V) \leftarrow \mathrm{Flag}(1,2;V) \rightarrow \mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ after Berkovich analytification. The Klein quadric $\mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ decomposes into the open orbit $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ and the Lagrangian quadric, which parametrize respectively the projective lines transverse and tangent to the standard contact distribution on $\mathbb{P}(V)$. We construct explicit free discrete subgroups $Γ\subset\mathrm{PSp}(V)$ and analytic domains, cut out by Drinfeld upper half-spaces, in all three members of the incidence diagram. Both incidence projections are surjective on these domains, the three $Γ$-actions are free and properly discontinuous, and the Penrose double correspondence descends to the analytic quotients. The quotient of the twistor domain is a contact analytic threefold, and the Grassmannian domain is contained in the analytification of the $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ open orbit.

entry.title: Kempe Reachability with $k\geq 3$ Colors Is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-Complete on Claw-Free Graphs
entry.summary: A \emph{proper vertex coloring} assigns colors to vertices so that adjacent vertices have distinct colors. A \emph{Kempe change} in a proper vertex coloring exchanges two colors on one component of the subgraph induced by the vertices of those colors. For a fixed palette of $k$ colors, \textsc{Kempe Reachability} asks whether two given proper vertex colorings of the same graph are connected by a sequence of Kempe changes. This problem is known to be $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. A graph is \emph{claw-free} if no vertex has three pairwise nonadjacent neighbors. The \emph{line graph} of a graph has one vertex for each edge, with two vertices adjacent exactly when the corresponding edges share an end. Line graphs are claw-free, and their Kempe changes correspond to \emph{edge-Kempe changes} in the original graph, which exchange two colors on one component of the subgraph formed by the edges of those colors. A claw-free graph with a proper $k$-coloring has maximum degree at most $2k-2$, whereas for $k\geq 4$ all proper $k$-colorings of a graph of maximum degree at most $k$ are connected by Kempe changes. We show that, for every fixed $k\geq 3$, \textsc{Kempe Reachability} with $k$ colors is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete even on line graphs of connected simple $k$-regular graphs, and hence even on connected $(2k-2)$-regular claw-free graphs. Equivalently, deciding whether two proper $k$-edge-colorings are connected by edge-Kempe changes is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete even on connected simple $k$-regular graphs. entry.title: Extra-dimensional Origins of Chemical Potentials at the Cosmological Collider
entry.summary: We study the realization of the chemical potential mechanism in cosmological collider physics in a robust class of inflationary models arising from multiple higher-dimensional gauge fields. The rolling inflaton background corresponds to an electric field in the extra dimension in which charged particles are produced analogously to the Schwinger mechanism, while neutral particles can be produced through non-minimal interactions. We show that particles heavier than the inflationary Hubble scale can be created without Boltzmann suppression in both cases. In particular, charged Kaluza-Klein excitations can be created through minimal gauge interactions. We construct realistic models along these lines consistent with both theoretical and experimental constraints.

entry.title: On Exact Critical-Region Boundaries in Continuous-Time Multiparametric Optimal Control Problems
entry.summary: Continuous-time multiparametric model predictive control solves the optimal control problem once, offline, for every initial state, and divides the initial-state space into critical regions, each with its own control law and sequence of active constraints. A boundary between two regions is either a hyperplane, given by one linear equation, or curved. The curved boundaries have not been computed to date; a classifier has been trained instead to distinguish the regions, so the partition has been known only approximately. In this paper we show that a curved boundary can be computed exactly, without solving any optimal control problem. The method rests on one property. Once the sequence of active constraints is fixed, together with the instants inside it at which a constraint becomes active or inactive (the switching times) and the instant at which the change of the neighboring region first appears (the event time), every condition on a boundary is a linear equation in the initial state, so the computation of a boundary, curved or not, is exact. We fix one of these instants, a switching time or the event time, and solve the linear equations that correspond to it for the corresponding initial state on the boundary; stepping the fixed instant along the horizon yields the whole boundary. A hyperplane is the case in which no instant is left to fix. We illustrate the method on the Newell-Lee evaporator, which has seven critical regions and eight boundaries, four hyperplanes and four curved, computing one boundary of each type in full with the adjacent regions at its ends.

entry.title: X-Dubbing: Speech-to-Speech Translation under Temporal and Visual Constraints
entry.summary: Cross-lingual dubbing aims to convert source speech into target-language speech that remains synchronized with the original video. The key to this task is to produce a faithful translation that is naturally speakable within the source timing, which is non-trivial because languages differ in duration, rhythm, and articulation. In this paper, we propose X-Dubbing, which formulates the task as a joint problem of time-aware speech-to-text translation and video-aware text-to-speech. Specifically, our method consists of a Dubbing Translator that generates temporally structured scripts and a Voice Actor that renders them in synchrony with the source video, both grounded in a language-agnostic timing budget. We further refine the translator with dubbing-aware feedback from the synthesized speech, encouraging scripts that yield well-synchronized dubbing. This design requires no paired dubbing data, as the two components are trained on speech-text and monolingual audio-visual data respectively. Extensive experiments show that X-Dubbing outperforms recent baselines across diverse metrics, including isochrony and audio-visual correspondence.

entry.title: PnP*: A certifiable solver for Perspective-n-Point
entry.summary: Estimating a camera pose from 3D-2D correspondences - Perspective-n-Point - is one of the most fundamental problems in computer vision. Existing methods either solve a minimal problem or replace the objective with an easier one. Surprisingly, no scalable certifiable solver for the actual Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) exists. We propose PnP*, the first practical solver that guarantees efficient computation and returns a certifiable globally optimal solution. We prove that the underlying convex relaxation is exact under moderate noise, which to our knowledge is the first stability guarantee for any relaxation for the MLE of PnP. Furthermore, we reduce the relaxation by exploiting chordal sparsity pattern and quotient ring reduction such that the relaxation is tractable and scalable. The stability and scalability results are verified numerically, as PnP* returns a provably correct camera pose at over 10 Hz.

entry.title: Capillary John ellipsoid theorem with applications to capillary curvature problems
entry.summary: In this paper, we apply a capillary John ellipsoid theorem for capillary convex bodies in the Euclidean half-space $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_{+}}$. This theorem yields a non-collapsing estimate for capillary hypersurfaces, which provides a new approach to obtaining $C^{0}$ estimates for solutions to some capillary curvature problems (including the capillary $L_{p}$ Christoffel-Minkowski problem and the capillary $L_{p}$ curvature problem), based on the corresponding gradient estimates. As an application, we study the capillary $L_{p}$ dual Minkowski problem. A gradient estimate, together with the non-collapsing estimate and a $C^2$ estimate, yields existence for every $1<p<q<\infty$ with positive smooth even data and an acute contact angle. The same estimates also yield the eigenvalue problem for $p=q>1$, with uniqueness up to dilation. We further obtain existence and uniqueness for $p>q$ without an upper restriction on $q$.

entry.title: Four-dimensional supersymmetric massive QED
entry.summary: We study a four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric Proca model with an explicit mass term for a real vector superfield and a generalized transverse kinetic operator. Although it displays no gauge redundancy in Proca variables, for local kinetic operators the model is the exact classical unitary-gauge form of the minimal Abelian $\mathcal N=1$ Stueckelberg realization, with the SQED-like exponential as its minimal gauge-covariant matter coupling. We compute the Kählerian contribution to the one-loop effective action using both the background-field Hessian and an independent supergraph organization. In the minimal model the background-dependent divergence is local and is absorbed by the matter Kähler normalization, and the finite local terms left by the subtraction remain scheme dependent. At $α=0$, an anomaly-free minimal Stueckelberg formulation supports a conditional perturbative-renormalizability interpretation for the corresponding minimal theory. For $f(\Box)=\Box+α\Box^2$ we distinguish the exact polynomial model, defined over the full momentum range, from a truncated derivative expansion; in the latter reading, the additional pole and the local matching term are ultraviolet information determined by the completion rather than predictions of the truncated theory.

entry.title: Facets of nondegeneracy: central type factor groups, Heisenberg representations and Hadamard matrices
entry.summary: Given a pair of complementary subgroups $P$ and $N$ of a finite group $G$, we first discuss how the same type of functions $\mathbb E\colon P\times N\to \mathbb T$, which we call bi-$1$-cocycles, appear naturally in the study of projective representations of $G$ of Heisenberg type and second cohomology of $G$ and of its dual quantum group $\widehat G$. We show then that such representations are irreducible and the corresponding ordinary and dual $2$-cocycles are nondegenerate if and only if the matrix $(\mathbb E(p,n))_{p,n}$ is invertible, if and only if it is Hadamard. We illustrate the result with examples arising from symplectic nilpotent Lie algebras over finite fields with two complementary Lagrangian subalgebras.

entry.title: Discorrelation of the Möbius function with linear phases in short intervals
entry.summary: We introduce a new approach to studying correlations between arithmetic functions and linear phases with respect to highly irrational frequencies over short intervals. As an application, we prove that \[ \Big|\sum_{x<n \leq x+H}μ(n) e(nα)\Big| \ll H(\log x)^{-1/3+\varepsilon } \] whenever $x^{0.58+\varepsilon }\leq H\leq x$. In the same range of $H$ we also show that \[ \Big|\sum_{x<n \leq x+H} Λ(n) e(nα)\Big| \ll H(\log x)^{-A} \] for arbitrarily large $A>0$ unless there exists an integer $1\leq q\ll (\log x)^{O_A(1)}$ such that $\|qα\| \ll x (\log x)^{O_A(1)}/H^2$. This breaks the $3/5$ barrier in Theorem 1.5 of arXiv:1911.09076v2 and Theorem 2 of [T. Zhan, "On the representation of large odd integer as a sum of three almost equal primes," Acta Mathematica Sinica 7.3 (1991), 259-272]. Moreover, by our method, any improvement in large value estimates for character-twisted Dirichlet polynomials on the critical range would lead to a corresponding improvement in the lower bound for $H$.

entry.title: Grey-body factor from correspondence with quasinormal mode for gravitational perturbation of higher-dimensional Reissner-Nordström black hole
entry.summary: We study the correspondence between quasinormal modes (QNMs) and grey-body factors (GBFs) of higher-dimensional Reissner--Nordström black holes. Considering scalar, vector, and tensor gravitational perturbations, we systematically compute the QNMs and GBFs for each spacetime dimension and set of black-hole parameters to evaluate the analytical formula connecting them. QNMs are obtained by the continued fraction and the integration-through-midpoints methods depending on the singularity structure in the Frobenius series. We compare the GBFs determined by the correspondence using QNMs with those computed numerically. The correspondence performs well for scalar($+$), vector($+$), vector($-$), and tensor perturbations. For the scalar($-$) perturbation, the GBFs obtained by the correspondence deviate noticeably from the accurate GBFs for black holes with low to intermediate values of the charge in $D>6$. The correspondence recovers reasonable accuracy at higher charges, although the effective potential exhibits double peaks, contrary to the assumption underlying the Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin (WKB)-based derivation of the correspondence. Whereas the accuracy decreases with increasing $D$ for other perturbation types, the correspondence for the scalar($-$) perturbation yields more accurate GBFs in $D=8$ than those in $D=7$. For near-extreme black holes, the correspondence offers a reliable approximation of GBFs for the vector($-$) perturbation, even though a double-peak potential occurs in $D>6$. These results suggest that the correspondence has a wider range of applicability than might be expected from the assumption of the WKB approach.

entry.title: Measuring, Localizing, and Reducing the AI-Like Writing Style of Post-Trained LLMs
entry.summary: Post-trained language models often exhibit a recognizable AI-like writing style, yet its connection to post-training and internal representations remains poorly understood. In this work, we study whether post-training introduces or amplifies AI-like stylistic regularities and whether these regularities have a localized internal signature. To this end, we compare human text, base-model generations, and aligned-model generations under matched human-source prefixes. Aligned generations show lower human-corpus affinity and higher AI-detection rates than base generations, suggesting that post-training shifts generated text away from human-corpus style and toward detector-visible AI-like text. We then introduce PASTA (Post-training Alignment Signature Targeted Ablation), a training-free method that estimates a post-training alignment signature from aligned-base residual contrasts and ablates the corresponding direction during decoding. Across 11 aligned models and 6 AI-detectors, PASTA lowers the detection rate for most aligned models; this effect transfers well across detectors and is not reproduced by random directions. Qualitative analysis suggests that PASTA generations remain relevant and coherent while exhibiting greater stylistic variation. Together, these results show that AI-like stylistic effects of post-training can be measured, localized, and causally tested through activation ablation.

entry.title: Typed Template Fuzzing
entry.summary: Fuzzing software with complex inputs has been a longstanding challenge. Traditionally, fuzzers either programmatically encode language constraints, requiring significant engineering effort, or rely on users to declare grammars and constraints. Recent LLM-based fuzzers address these drawbacks but introduce new issues. Some use LLMs for test generation, sacrificing throughput and producing invalid inputs when the LLM makes mistakes. Others rely on language-specific parsers, static analysis, and AST manipulation libraries. We introduce Typed Template Fuzzing (TTF), a lightweight LLM-based fuzzing methodology. The key idea is to use LLMs in a preprocessing step to transform seeds into typed templates. The typed templates then enable semantically aware, mutation-based fuzzing without language-specific parsers, type checkers, or further LLM queries during fuzzing. By exploiting the correspondence between seeds and templates, TTF can moreover repair LLM mistakes. We have implemented TTF in our tool Typos, which we evaluate across 21 input languages, including C, C++, Go, Rust, SystemVerilog, Scala, and Java, as well as libraries such as PyTorch and Qiskit. In a six-month fuzzing campaign, we reported 135 bugs, 128 of which were previously unknown. Perhaps most notably, on average 96% of Typos's mutants are valid, coming close to the validity rates of domain-specific fuzzers. Our evaluation further shows Typos's benefits over the state of the art.

entry.title: ReCoG: Relational Concept Graph for Training-Free Personalization
entry.summary: Training-free personalization adapts a frozen vision-language model (VLM) to recognize user-defined concepts from only a few exemplars by retrieving concept entries at inference time. While recent retriever-based methods enrich each concept with descriptive evidence, they largely treat concepts in isolation, so the retrieved information can be plausible yet non-discriminative, especially when the personalized concept set contains highly confusable, fine-grained categories. We argue that personalization is inherently relational: correct recognition depends on the specific distinctions between a concept and its nearest alternatives. To this end, we propose ReCoG, a Relational Concept Graph for retrieval-augmented personalization. ReCoG represents concepts as nodes and augments them with directed edges that explicitly capture discriminative cues between concept pairs, elicited by a frozen VLM during database construction. At inference, ReCoG retrieves a shortlist and resolves ambiguity via explicit pairwise comparisons conditioned on the corresponding relational edges, selecting the concept that consistently wins against competing candidates. We also introduce FINGER benchmark to test personalized recognition on confusable concept sets. Across FINGER, ReCoG substantially outperforms prior methods, with the largest gains in the most confusable regimes. ReCoG also achieves consistently best performance on established personalization benchmarks including captioning and VQA, confirming that relational evidence is broadly beneficial beyond fine-grained settings. Project Page: https://csy-98.github.io/ReCoG/

entry.title: Telling Neural Network What We Know: Weight Configuration for RNN and Its Application to NextG Real-Time Neural Receiver
entry.summary: AI-enabled receivers offer a promising approach to adaptive physical-layer processing, but conventional neural receivers often require extensive offline training and computationally expensive backpropagation, limiting their suitability for low-latency cellular systems. Moreover, classical MIMO-OFDM receivers rely on accurate channel estimation, leading to substantial pilot overhead. This paper introduces skip-RNN, a lightweight skip-augmented recurrent neural receiver that performs online time-domain receive processing using fixed recurrent and skip branches with an adaptive linear readout. We show that the skip-RNN can be interpreted as a structured deconvolution filter whose recurrent and skip branches realize IIR and FIR basis functions, respectively. We develop a domain-knowledge informed weight-configuration framework for the skip-RNN by exploiting its structural correspondence with the target stable and causal inverse filter of mixed-phase channels. The dominant IIR structure extracted from estimated channel statistics is used to configure the recurrent dynamics, while the non-minimum-phase component is addressed through the skip branch and a statistical FIR readout prior incorporated into prior-centered regularized online readout adaptation. We further derive an approximation-error bound that characterizes the resulting configured neural-receiver representation. Simulations over standardized 3GPP channels demonstrate the effectiveness of the configured neural receiver under extremely low pilot overhead.

entry.title: A Diagnostic for Bias in Linear Mixed Model Estimators Induced by Dependence Between the Random Effects and the Corresponding Model Matrix
entry.summary: We explore how violations of the often-overlooked standard assumption that the random effects model matrix in a linear mixed model is fixed (and thus independent of the random effects vector) can lead to bias in estimators of estimable functions of the fixed effects. However, if the random effects of the original mixed model are instead also treated as fixed effects, or if the fixed and random effects model matrices are orthogonal with respect to the inverse of the error covariance matrix (with probability one), or if the random effects and the corresponding model matrix are independent, then these estimators are unbiased. The bias in the general case is quantified, and a diagnostic for its random-effects contribution is compared to a randomized permutation distribution of the predicted random effects, producing an informative summary graphic for each estimator of interest. This is demonstrated through the examination of sporting outcomes used to estimate a home field advantage.

entry.title: Bounded symbols and one-component geometry
entry.summary: We prove that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on a Hardy model space admits a bounded symbol if and only if its defining inner function is one-component, meaning that it has a connected sublevel set at some level in $(0,1)$. This resolves the bounded symbol conjecture of Baranov, Chalendar, Fricain, Mashreghi and Timotin and, through known equivalences, the embedding and weak factorization conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin. A uniform bound $R$ for the ratio of least bounded symbol norm to operator norm on the rank-one family associated with point evaluation in the disk already forces this geometry. The corresponding bound for all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators is at most $CR\log(e+R)$, where $C$ is absolute, and the logarithmic factor is optimal. In a nonzero de Branges space, the same geometric condition characterizes when every sufficiently small equivalent change of norm preserving the de Branges structure is represented exactly by reweighting the original integral with a positive density bounded above and away from zero. This characterization remains valid when the norm changes are restricted to discrete sampling norms. Outside the one-component class, every model space admits self-adjoint trace class truncated Toeplitz operators without bounded symbols, with arbitrarily small norm and singular values satisfying any prescribed positive upper bounds.

entry.title: Mixed State Deep Thermalization under Generic Quantum Errors
entry.summary: Pure-state deep thermalization predicts that, after sufficient scrambling, projected ensembles approach universal distributions that contain information beyond the reduced density matrix. In realistic quantum systems, however, noise is unavoidable and the projected states are generally mixed. Whether mixed-state deep thermalization admits an analogous universal limiting distribution has remained unclear. Here we answer this question for quantum dynamics containing local quantum channels, i.e., errors. We show that the late-time mixed-state projected ensemble is completely determined by the normalized Choi state of the error channel and is universal, independent of the microscopic details of the underlying unitary dynamics. We establish this result analytically for dual-unitary circuits, global Haar-random dynamics, and local Haar-random circuits at large local dimension, and verify it numerically in qubit circuits and kicked Ising dynamics. In a solvable setting, we further find exponentially fast convergence to the limiting ensemble. Our results extend deep thermalization to noisy quantum dynamics and establish a direct correspondence between quantum errors and universal random mixed-state ensembles.

entry.title: Biases in gaps between zeros of Dirichlet L-functions
entry.summary: We describe a new family of Dirichlet L-functions that provably have an unusual value distribution. Experimentally, we find that the L-functions in this family have a significant and previously undetected bias in the distribution of gaps between their zeros. These phenomena appear to have an arithmetic explanation that corresponds to the nonvanishing of a certain Gauss-type sum. We give a complete classification of the characters for which this sum is nonzero and count them. This sum vanishes for 100% of primitive Dirichlet characters, so L-functions in our newly discovered family are rare (a set of density zero among all primitive characters). The nonvanishing of this sum implies that there is a main term when one integrates the Z-function associated to a Dirichlet L-function over a long interval. We prove that the L-functions in this family are the only GL(1)/Q or GL(2)/Q cuspidal automorphic L-functions whose Z-functions have a "large" mean value when integrated. We discuss analogous results for the Riemann zeta-function.

entry.title: Affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequalities and optimal star bodies
entry.summary: In this paper, we establish an affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequality by replacing the Euclidean fractional Orlicz seminorm with an energy obtained by minimizing over origin-symmetric star bodies of prescribed volume. Under finite lower and upper power growth assumptions, a subcritical upper growth bound, and a monotonicity condition on $t^{n/s+2}Φ''(t)$, the resulting inequality has the same best constant as its Euclidean counterpart. The power case recovers the affine fractional Sobolev inequality of Haddad and Ludwig with the corresponding Luxemburg normalization. To establish this inequality, we investigate the underlying geometric extremal problem. For every nonzero smooth function of compact support, the existence and uniqueness of an optimal star body are proved under the growth assumptions alone, and its radial function is characterized by an equation involving $Φ(t)+(s/n)tΦ'(t)$. We also establish an anisotropic rearrangement inequality, together with its equality conditions under additional strictness assumptions. Moreover, the normalized local limit is investigated. The optimized energies converge to the local energy, and the radial functions of the minimizing bodies converge uniformly on the sphere. The limiting modular is determined by $\overlineΦ(t)=\int_0^tΦ(τ)\,dτ/τ$. Finally, we compare optimization over star bodies with optimization in the affine orbit.

entry.title: DBCM: Dual-Branch Calibration Module for Test-Time Adaptation in Time Series Forecasting
entry.summary: Non-stationarity induces test-time distribution shifts in time series forecasting (TSF), resulting in forecast residuals between predictions and the corresponding ground truth. Recent works on test-time adaptation for TSF address this by introducing lightweight calibration modules around frozen forecasters, updated using observations that become incrementally available at test time. Existing approaches typically employ channel-wise adapters, implicitly assuming that forecast residuals are inherently channel-specific. However, we observe that forecast residuals often exhibit substantial shared structure across channels, suggesting that fully independent channel-wise parameterization may be redundant. Motivated by this observation, we propose the Dual-Branch Calibration Module (DBCM), which shares adaptation capacity across channels through a shared adapter while retaining limited channel-specific flexibility through a low-rank channel-wise adapter, further enhanced by channel mixing and nonlinear gated modulation. Extensive experiments show that DBCM consistently outperforms prior methods across diverse datasets, horizons, and backbones.

entry.title: Are LLM-Generated Formal Specifications Faithful to Their Requirements? A Study on Bimodal Formal Specification Generation
entry.summary: Formal specification generation is a critical step towards formal verification and correctness assurance of software. Recently, large language models have been widely adopted in automatic generation of formal specifications. However, existing LLM-based specification generation approaches often assume that the input program is correct, which deviates from the real purpose of formal verification---to figure out whether the program meets its requirements when its correctness is unknown. Therefore, we conduct an empirical study of LLM-based specification generation under the bimodal setting: given both the natural language requirement and its corresponding code implementation, whose correctness is unknown. We construct a benchmark of 1,403 C programs and evaluate ACSL specification generation with Frama-C verification. Our study reaches several interesting findings: first, when the code implementation is correct, providing the natural language requirement does not further improve the pass rate of generated specifications. Second, when the code implementation is incorrect, LLM-based specification generation may erroneously pass verification by producing weak or implementation-misled specifications, and this cannot be fully alleviated by advanced prompting approaches. Compared with the non-formal HoarePrompt approach, LLM-generated formal specifications are less effective in predicting requirement-code consistency. Our study takes a first look at applying LLM-based formal specification generation to verifying program correctness against requirements, and points to requirement-faithful specification generation as a new direction for future LLM-based formal specification research.

entry.title: Piecewise $P_2$ finite element space on rectangular meshes in arbitrary dimensions for the biharmonic equation
entry.summary: This paper develops a piecewise $P_2$ finite element space on rectangular meshes in arbitrary dimensions for the biharmonic equation. The discrete space imposes continuity of vertex sums on $(d-2)$-faces and of averaged normal derivatives across interior $(d-1)$-faces. A local algebraic characterization of $P_2$ is first established through the unisolvence of an enriched polynomial space and the resulting compatibility conditions. For each interior element, a $3^d$-element patch is then introduced, and the associated homogeneous patch space is shown to be one-dimensional. The corresponding patch functions, extended by zero, form a basis of the global homogeneous discrete space. A local quadratic interpolation operator is further constructed in arbitrary dimensions. Its approximation properties, together with a consistency estimate derived from the weak continuity conditions, lead to the optimal broken $H^2$ error estimate for the biharmonic problem.

entry.title: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
entry.summary: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.

entry.title: Melonic ladder holography with a single free bulk field in AdS$_{d+1}$
entry.summary: We derive a cylinder from the pair Casimir of a CFT$_d$: at zero centre momentum it depends only on relative dilations and rotations. Relative-coordinate radial quantisation then encodes exchanged family labels as cylinder energies. For a melonic CFT$_d$ in the normalisable and stable range, the reduced ladder sum is the Robin boundary-to-boundary propagator of a single free scalar field in rigid AdS$_{d+1}$, with the cylinder as its conformal boundary. The Robin boundary condition and bulk regularity (or parity) determine the holographic radial extension of the boundary data. A nonzero Robin boundary coefficient in global AdS breaks $2d$ AdS generators, yet the scalar's boundary propagator still encodes the conformal data of the melonic ladder. We demonstrate the correspondence for the Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev and the $d=2$ disorder-free long-range Amit--Roginsky melonic models, which correspond to a single free local scalar in AdS$_2$ and AdS$_3$, respectively.

entry.title: On perfectoid ideals
entry.summary: In this paper, we study perfectoid ideals using the reduction modulo $p$ of perfectoid rings. We show that perfectoid ideals correspond to ideals in the reduction modulo $p$ on which Frobenius is surjective. We establish the existence of universal $p$-adic power series whose evaluations, together with their compatible $p$-power roots, generate perfectoidizations of ideals. In the special case of the perfectoidization of $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/p^{\infty}}\rangle/(t-1)$, we describe a linear algebra algorithm for computing finite approximations of such generators. We illustrate this by an explicit approximation modulo $8$ of an element $σ\in (t-1)_{\mathrm{perfd}}\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_2^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/2^{\infty}}\rangle$ which admits compatible sequences of $2$-power roots and satisfies $σ\equiv t-1\pmod{2}$.

entry.title: The Galactic Center Reference Frame: A 30-Year Solution
entry.summary: Stellar orbits probe the metric of and mass around the Sgr A* massive black hole. To enable study of the black hole, the surrounding mass, and tests of gravity, a precise reference frame must be established and maintained. We present an updated stellar maser-based reference frame for the inner parsec of the Galactic Center, referenced to the radio continuum of Sgr A*. This work synthesizes 30 years of astrometric observations of 15 SiO stellar masers and the Sgr A* continuum at 43 GHz. The uncertainty in the mean offset of the maser ensemble from Sgr A* is 0.08 mas in the current epoch and will decay to 0.10 mas by 2030. At a distance of 8.2 kpc, these correspond to position uncertainties of 0.6 AU and 0.8 AU, respectively, which is similar to or smaller than the stellar SiO-emitting region. The mean maser proper motion uncertainties are 0.05 mas yr$^{-1}$ in RA and 0.08 mas yr$^{-1}$ in Dec, corresponding to 1.8 km s$^{-1}$ and 3.2 km s$^{-1}$. The reference frame stability between IR and maser astrometry is 10~$μ$as yr$^{-1}$ (0.40 km s$^{-1}$) in RA and 15 $μ$as yr$^{-1}$ (0.57 km s$^{-1}$) in Dec. The masers show substantial variability in flux density and velocity structure, most notably IRS~7, which shows a 30-fold brightening in a blueshifted component since 2022. This variability may set a floor on future astrometry improvements and especially measurements of radial acceleration.

entry.title: SO(5) multicriticality in two-dimensional quantum magnets
entry.summary: We resolve the nature of the quantum phase transition between antiferromagnetic and valence-bond solid ground states in square-lattice spin-1/2 magnets - the putative deconfined quantum-critical point. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations of J-Q models, in which Heisenberg exchange J competes with multi-spin interactions Qn formed by n singlet projectors, we demonstrate first-order discontinuities increasing with n. For n=2 and n=3, the first-order signatures are very weak and we extract universal scaling dimensions of a proximate multicritical point. Their values coincide closely with known bounds for an SO(5) symmetric conformal field theory (CFT) containing a relevant SO(5) singlet operator that destabilizes the generic deconfined critical point. We characterize the emergent SO(5) symmetry by its scaling dimensions of the leading irrelevant perturbations. Using the J-Q2-Q6 model, we tune the transition from weak to stronger first-order and find scaling of the coexisting order parameters with a large exponent beta ~ 0.85, in agreement with the relevant scaling dimensions of the multicritical point. The exponent that had previously been identified with the correlation length does not have a corresponding CFT level, and we explain it as pseudo-critical length scale of bubbles of one phase inside the other that are compressed in size by an SO(5)-violating irrelevant repulsive interaction between the two order parameters. The bubble scale reflects a hierarchy of excitation gaps generated by the SO(5) perturbation in the neighborhood of the first-order transition, akin to a Higgs mechanism. We argue that the multicritical point is the tip of a gapless spin liquid phase in frustrated Heisenberg models into which the J-Q models can be deformed, but the spin liquid, and perhaps the multicritical point itself, exist outside the regime amenable to sign-free simulations.

entry.title: Universal Inference for Testing Calibration and Specification of Mean Estimates within the Exponential Dispersion Family
entry.summary: Calibration of mean estimates is a crucial property in many applications, particularly in actuarial decision-making. Tests of mean-calibration are often performed under the assumption that the estimated means correctly preserve the ordering of the corresponding population means. In this paper, we first consider the classical Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT) within the Exponential Dispersion Family (EDF), and we show that applying likelihood-based methods to test mean-calibration within the EDF requires a strong ordering assumption on the mean estimates. This assumption makes the null hypothesis of the mean-calibration test equivalent to the correct specification of the mean estimates. Next, we investigate the framework of universal inference for testing mean-calibration and mean-specification, and the relationship between the tests. We develop a sub-sampled split LRT within the EDF that provides finite-sample guarantees with universally valid critical values. We investigate type I error, power, and e-power of the sub-sampled split LRT and compare its performance with that of the classical LRT. We also propose a novel test statistic based on a sub-sampled split $L_q$-likelihood ratio test (L$q$RT) to enhance the performance of the statistical test. Numerical results demonstrate that universal inference based on the sub-sampled split LRT and sub-sampled split L$q$RT provides an attractive alternative to the classical LRT within the EDF, achieving high power for detecting miscalibration and misspecification in medium- and large-sized samples.

entry.title: Dynamics of the Density Cube
entry.summary: Density cube theory extends the canonical quantum density matrix $ρ_{ij}$ with the addition of an extra index to $ρ_{ijk}$. The elements of the density cube with two different indices, $ρ_{iij}$ and $ρ_{ijj}$, correspond to the real and imaginary parts of the off-diagonal element $ρ_{ij}$ of the density matrix and describe double-path interference, while those with three different indices describe non-canonical triple-path interference. In this letter, we propose an equation of motion for the density cube, obtained from the quantization of ternary Nambu dynamics, and find that pairs of triple-path interferences oscillate into each other.

entry.title: Unifying description of competing chiral and nematic superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene
entry.summary: We reveal a striking correspondence between electron- and phonon-driven pairing in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) by mapping an atomistic electronically driven pairing model onto an effective inter-valley, intra-Chern description, originally proposed for phonon-mediated superconductivity. Within the unified framework of intra-Chern pairing, we then analyze the competition between nematic and chiral $d$-wave superconducting states. The latter corresponds to the extreme Chern-polarized limit and hosts unpaired flat bands within the superconducting gap, which generally disfavors it relative to the nematic states. Crucially, nematic order is locally preferred at each momentum, but the optimal nematic directions are incompatible across the Brillouin zone due to the broken rotation symmetry. This momentum-space frustration still enables a chiral ground state at large fillings or weak interactions in a symmetric parent state. Including heterostrain or inter-valley coherence further stabilizes the nematic ground state and sets the nematic direction. Under heterostrain, this direction shows a double winding with the strain axis, revealing the $d$-wave nature of the pairing, while inter-valley coherence makes it filling dependent. Our results thereby provide a unified understanding of superconductivity in TBG, in which electron- and phonon-mediated pairing cooperate, and clarify the microscopic origin of the competition between the chiral and nematic superconducting states.

entry.title: Affine Higher Bruhat Orders
entry.summary: The higher Bruhat orders are partial orders originally constructed by Manin and Schechtman, with an equivalent construction from Ziegler. These partial orders generalize the weak order on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$, and the second higher Bruhat order is a poset on commutation classes of reduced words for the longest element in ${\mathfrak{S}}_n$, where covering relations correspond to braid relations. Like the weak order, each of the higher Bruhat orders is a ranked poset with unique minimal and maximal elements. Constructing analogs of the higher Bruhat orders in other settings is an area of recent interest, including recent work of Hothem for permutations in $S_{n}$. We give a construction that generalizes any interval $[\mathrm{id},w]$ in the weak order where $w$ is an element of the affine symmetric group $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$. Our construction recovers the classical higher Bruhat orders when $w$ is the longest element in $\mathfrak{S}_n$. Paralleling the classical case, we show that the second higher Bruhat order is a ranked poset on commutation classes of reduced words for $w\in \widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$, allowing us to prove a conjecture due to Elias. When $w\in \mathfrak{S}_n$, we also establish results for our higher Bruhat orders that are direct analogs of numerous results in the classical higher Bruhat orders.

entry.title: Erdős-Sós via random cyclic orderings
entry.summary: We present a simplified proof of the Erdős-Sós conjecture on trees in graphs, which is based on its recent resolution by GPT-6 Astra. At the same time, we also give another proof of the corresponding conjecture for antidirected trees in digraphs, posed by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares Sales, Reed, and Thomassé, and we simplify recent proofs of Kalai's conjecture for tight trees in hypergraphs. Our proof uses the language of random cyclic orderings in order to take advantage of symmetries that were obscured in the original argument, and we hope that the reader will find it intuitive. We also characterize the extremal examples for Kalai's conjecture, and we generalize it to the setting of so-called fully directed $r$-uniform hypergraphs, whose edges are ordered $r$-tuples.

entry.title: Roto-Reflection Geometry of Pure Two-Qubit Entanglement
entry.summary: Pure two-qubit entanglement is usually characterized by scalar quantities such as concurrence. Here we show that it also has a natural geometric form. In the Pauli correlation tensor, maximally entangled states appear as improper orthogonal maps between two local Bloch spheres. These maps are roto-reflections. For partially entangled pure states, the same roto-reflection geometry is recovered after separating the contraction associated with concurrence. We call the corresponding geometric object the Entanglement Roto-Reflection Plane (ERRP). It organizes the maximally correlated directions of the two-qubit state and provides a covariant geometric complement to the scalar magnitude of entanglement. We further illustrate the usefulness of this geometry through partial transposition, where it provides a direct construction of the maximally entangled negative eigenvector and a geometric interpretation of negativity.

entry.title: Linear causality and stability constraints on relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics
entry.summary: In this work, we construct a theoretical framework for relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics based on entropy current analysis. The formalism consistently incorporates finite relaxation dynamics of the dissipative fluxes, providing a transient framework suitable for analyzing linear stability and short-wavelength causality. Utilizing linear mode analysis, we investigate the constraints imposed by causality and stability on this anisotropic system. By linearizing the theory around a homogeneous equilibrium state, we identify the magnetosonic, Alfvén, and charge-diffusion sectors, together with their coupling terms. For each sector, we derive asymptotic dispersion relations in both the long-wavelength (small-$k$) and short-wavelength (large-$k$) regimes, validating them against exact numerical roots. Our numerical analysis confirms the accuracy of these asymptotic solutions and uncovers a nontrivial angular dependence, especially near special propagation directions where the ordinary momentum expansion becomes less reliable. By evaluating the large-$k$ behavior of the propagating branches alongside the damping properties of non-hydrodynamic modes, we delineate the corresponding causality constraints. We find that the admissible linear causal domain is governed by the interplay between propagation direction, anisotropic transport coefficients, and relaxation times, with the resulting bounds being intrinsically mode-dependent. These findings provide a systematic theoretical basis for investigating linear stability and short-wavelength causality in relativistic magnetohydrodynamics beyond the first-order approximation.

entry.title: Fewer simulations, sharper covariances: Reducing mock covariance noise with Zeldovich approximation control variates
entry.summary: We present a control-variate method for reducing the variance of power spectrum covariance matrix estimates from simulations of large-scale structure. The idea is to pair each mock simulation with a cheap Zeldovich-approximation realization sharing the same initial conditions, and to use the known statistical properties of the Zeldovich field to remove correlated sample variance from the covariance estimator. Under a Gaussian disconnected approximation, we derive fully analytic expressions for both the optimal control-variate coefficient, $β(k,\ell;k',\ell')$, and the corresponding correlation, $ρ(k,\ell;k',\ell')$, in terms of the auto- and cross-power spectra of the target and control fields. In the monopole case, the correlation takes the simple form $ρ(k,k') = r^2(k),r^2(k')$, where $r(k)$ is the standard cross-correlation coefficient between the target and Zeldovich fields, implying that covariance estimation remains highly efficient whenever the two fields are strongly correlated. For masked redshift-space lognormal mocks, resembling LRGs from DESI, we find that the control-variate estimator reduces the variance of the covariance matrix by approximately an order of magnitude on large scales, $k\lesssim 0.05\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, precisely where accurate covariance estimation is most challenging. The gains are smaller for higher $k$ but typically accelerate convergence by a factor of 2-3, substantially lowering the computational cost of covariance estimation for current and upcoming large-scale structure surveys. After a cheap parametric-bootstrap calibration of the precision-matrix bias, the control-variate covariance yields a $χ^2$ distribution consistent with the expected number of degrees of freedom. This method is readily implementable in current imaging and spectroscopic surveys (e.g., DESI, \textit{Euclid}, LSST, PFS, \textit{SPHEREx}).

entry.title: GelSlim 5.0: Unifying Vision and Touch with a Single Fingertip Camera
entry.summary: Vision and touch provide complementary cues for object pose and local contact geometry, but external cameras are often occluded at the contact site. We present GelSlim 5.0, a fingertip sensor that acquires visual and tactile observations with one fixed camera and a continuous UV-responsive contact layer. By switching illumination, the camera sequentially acquires through-membrane visual images and contact-sensitive tactile images from a shared viewpoint, avoiding inter-camera extrinsic calibration. To combine these observations, we introduce VisTacFusion, a multimodal transformer with separate prediction paths for planar object pose and contact geometry. Asymmetric bottleneck fusion incorporates visual context while preserving tactile spatial features for depth and surface-normal estimation. Modality dropout enables inference with paired inputs or either modality alone. On real validation data from 12 known objects, paired inputs reduce depth MSE, angular error, and translation $L_1$ by 61.2%, 72.3%, and 61.3%, respectively, relative to tactile-only inference with the same model. Relative to visual-only inference, the corresponding reductions are 93.7%, 6.1%, and 8.6%.

entry.title: Mathematical AI Predicts 40% and 57% Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Against H1N1 and H3N2, Respectively, for the 2026--2027 U.S. Season
entry.summary: Background: Clinical influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) has often been low over the past two decades, highlighting the need for preseason VE forecasting. Timely forecasts could help health authorities plan prevention strategies and allocate healthcare resources. However, preseason forecasting of clinical influenza VE remains relatively uncommon. Methods: We obtained hemagglutinin (HA) sequences from GISAID for U.S. specimens collected in August--September before each influenza season from 2010--2011 through 2024--2025. After quality screening, we compared each virus with the corresponding vaccine target strain for the same season and subtype or lineage using two mathematical distances based on amino acid patterns in the HA protein. We calculated mean distances for each season and subtype or lineage and paired them with published clinical VE estimates, yielding 26 observations across 13 seasons. Using a mathematical AI approach, we fitted linear regression models of VE against each distance and evaluated their predictive performance by forecasting later seasons using data from earlier seasons, with the historical mean VE for each subtype or lineage as a reference. We then applied the same approach to 87 HA sequences collected in August--September 2026 to forecast VE for the 2026--2027 season. Results: We generated component-specific forecasts of influenza VE for the upcoming 2026--2027 U.S. season. Both mathematical distances were negatively associated with historical VE, indicating that greater differences between circulating viruses and vaccine strains were associated with lower VE. The topological model forecast VE of 40.3%, 56.9%, and 47.1% against A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria, respectively, whereas the geometric model forecast corresponding VE values of 34.0%, 56.8%, and 51.1%.

entry.title: Rank-One Loss Maximizes the Spectral Response Strength of Passive Full-Order Exceptional Points
entry.summary: We consider finite-dimensional non-Hermitian systems in which all modes coalesce at a single exceptional point. For a rank-one anti-Hermitian contribution, the spectral response strength is computed exactly. For passive systems, we then derive a sharp upper bound at fixed exceptional-point decay rate and show that it is reached only when the decay operator has rank one, corresponding to a single independent dissipative direction. This establishes rank-one loss as the optimal configuration for enhancing the response of a full-order exceptional point. The bound holds for arbitrary order and improves on earlier passive estimates beyond second order. Two third-order trimers illustrate the result: a rank-one-loss system saturates the bound, whereas a passive rank-two-loss realization remains below it. The result turns dissipation into a design resource: concentrating the loss into a single effective dissipative direction maximizes the highest-order spectral response of a passive full-order exceptional-point device.

entry.title: Positive sectional curvature on exotic spheres in infinitely many dimensions
entry.summary: We show that there exist exotic spheres with metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature in infinitely many dimensions: in every dimension $n\equiv3\pmod4$ with $n\geq11$ and $n\not\equiv255\pmod{256}$. Previously, every known closed simply connected manifold of positive sectional curvature in a dimension above $24$ was diffeomorphic to a compact rank-one symmetric space. The spheres we consider are certain homotopy spheres arising as quotients of special $S^3$-$S^3$ bundles introduced by Sperança. These homotopy spheres are determined by an orthogonal representation $ρ$ of $S^3$ and an $S^3$-conjugation-equivariant map $β$, and are denoted $Σ_{ρ,β}$. By recent constructions, such spheres admit Riemannian metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature. In this paper we consider the spheres $Σ_{ρ_b,β}$ of dimension $4b+3$, $b\geq2$, where $ρ_b$ is the representation of $S^3$ on $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathbb{H}^b$ by left multiplication on the second summand. For these spheres, we show that the Eells-Kuiper invariant is the product of an integer $k(β)$ depending only on $β$ and a rational number $r_b$ given by one coefficient of a power series built from the $\hat A$- and $L$-genera. We then show that, for every $b\geq2$ with $b\not\equiv63\pmod{64}$, there is a map $β$ for which the Eells-Kuiper invariant does not vanish, and thus the corresponding sphere is exotic. A computer calculation also gives the dimensions $n\equiv255\pmod{256}$ below $2^{16}$.

entry.title: Unexpected Local Enhancement of Chromospheric Moreton Waves on the Sun
entry.summary: Solar eruptions often drive shock waves. When propagating in the solar corona, strong shock waves would leave imprints on the solar surface in the chromosphere, which are called Moreton waves. Moreton waves generally decay as they move away. However, to our knowledge, for the first time we report that a Moreton wave is significantly enhanced midway during propagation, as revealed by the spectroscopic observations from China's first solar satellite, the Chinese H$α$ Solar Explorer. Combining magnetic measurements from the Solar Dynamics Observatory, we found that the location of the Moreton wave enhancement corresponds to a magnetic null point at an altitude of $\sim$70 Mm in the corona. It is demonstrated that the unexpected local enhancement of the Moreton wave is due to mode conversion around the magnetic null point, i.e., fast-mode waves are converted to slow-mode waves which are trapped locally. It is further revealed that, even for ordinary Moreton wave fronts, the H$α$ Doppler redshift velocity is positively correlated with the height of widespread low-altitude magnetic null points, implying that these low-lying null points, $\sim$1--7 Mm above the solar surface, facilitate mode conversion with different efficiency, thereby accounting for the spatially inhomogeneous Dopplergram of Moreton wave fronts.

entry.title: Cluster scattering diagrams of acyclic affine type
entry.summary: We give an explicit construction of the cluster scattering diagram for any acyclic exchange matrix of affine type. We show that the corresponding cluster scattering fan coincides both with the mutation fan and with a fan constructed in the almost-positive roots model.

entry.title: On invariant $1$-dimensional representations of a finite $W$-algebra
entry.summary: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra over $\mathbf{C}$ and $G$ be the corresponding simply connected algebraic group. Consider a nilpotent element $e\in \mathfrak{g}$, the corresponding element $χ=(e, \bullet)$ in $\mathfrak{g}^*$, and the coadjoint orbit $\mathbf{O}=Gχ$. We are interested in the set $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$ of codimension $1$ ideals $J\subset \mathcal{W}$ in a finite $W$-algebra $\mathcal{W}=U(\mathfrak{g}, e)$. We have a natural action of the component group $Γ=Z_G(χ)/Z_G^\circ(χ)$ on $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$. Denote the set of $Γ$-stable points of $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$ by $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^{1}(\mathcal{W})^Γ$. For a classical $\mathfrak{g}$ Premet and Topley proved that $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^{1}(\mathcal{W})^Γ$ are parameterized by the points of an affine space. In this paper we will give an alternative proof of this fact using completely different approach. As a corollary of our construction, we imply that for classical $\mathfrak{g}$ all $Γ$-invariant $1$-dimensional representations of $\mathcal{W}$ are obtained by a parabolic induction introduced by Losev.

entry.title: The classical two-loop amplitude at leading logarithmic accuracy for graviton emission in multi-Regge kinematics
entry.summary: Using the gravitational shockwave formalism, we compute the classical part of the $\mathcal{O}(G^{7/2})$ five-point amplitude at leading logarithmic accuracy describing the emission of a graviton in the collision of two massless scalars in multi-Regge kinematics (MRK). The result splits into a two-particle reducible term and a three-particle reducible one, the latter being the radiative counterpart of the $H$-diagram with the emission taken in MRK limit. The same amplitude can be equivalently calculated as the ultrarelativistic limit of the corresponding massive amplitude by applying the optical theorem according to the conjectured universality of the leading logarithmic amplitudes in classical gravity.

entry.title: Hardness and Approximation for Compressing Deterministic Finite Automata
entry.summary: The delayed deterministic finite automaton ($\text{D}^2\text{FA}$) is a powerful tool for compressing the prohibitively large deterministic finite automata (DFAs) used in modern signature-based deep packet inspection systems. A $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$ augments a DFA with unlabeled default transitions to remove transitions that are similar. This technique works well in practice and has inspired numerous subsequent studies. However, existing approaches do not guarantee a $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$ of optimal size as they restrict the default transitions to form a forest. In this paper, we consider the problem of finding an optimal $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$. We make the key observation that cycles of default transitions can be valid and produce a smaller $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$, provided that for every character in the alphabet, at least one state in the cycle has an outgoing transition labeled by that character. This observation raises fundamental questions concerning the computational complexity of finding an optimal $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$ and the approximation guarantee of the standard (forest-restricted) approach. We answer both questions by showing that it is NP-hard to find an optimal $\text{D}^2\text{FA}$ and by proving that the standard approach provides a $3/2$-approximation to the optimum. To establish NP-hardness, we construct a reduction from set cover using a DFA with gadgets where valid default transition choices correspond to selecting sets. To prove our approximation ratio, we compare the cycles in an optimal solution to a variant where the default transitions form a forest. Finally, we demonstrate that this $3/2$ ratio is tight via a constructed family of DFAs.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks vs U-Net: Application to thermal dust emission recovery in the microwave
entry.summary: Galactic thermal dust emission is the dominant foreground contaminant of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) at frequencies above 100 GHz, and its accurate separation is essential for current and future CMB experiments. Deep learning methods, in particular convolutional architectures such as the U-Net, have demonstrated strong performance for CMB component separation, but typically operate as purely data-driven models with no explicit enforcement of the physical laws governing the emission they reconstruct. In this work, we present a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) that embeds the Modified Black Body (MBB) spectral model as a hard, differentiable architectural constraint, and we compare it against a standard U-Net baseline trained under an identical pipeline. Both architectures are trained on realistic simulated Planck HFI patches at four frequencies (143, 217, 353 and 545 GHz) and evaluated on a shared validation set as well as on three independent Galactic dust realizations from the PySM phenomenological dust models named D4, D7 and D10. We find that both networks achieve comparable reconstruction quality across all evaluated datasets, with a Structural Similarity Index Measure consistently above 0.96 and a fitted angular power-spectrum spectral index that agrees with the input to within 1% in every region. Embedding the physical constraint in the PINN does not measurably degrade reconstruction accuracy relative to the unconstrained U-Net, while additionally guaranteeing that every predicted output corresponds to a thermodynamically admissible physical configuration. These results establish the physics-informed formulation as a viable methodological alternative for dust component separation, providing physical interpretability without a trade-off in reconstruction fidelity.

entry.title: Degenerations of Jordan algebras
entry.summary: We describe all degenerations of complex $4$-dimensional Jordan algebras and of complex $5$-dimensional nilpotent Jordan algebras. The proofs do not use other papers on degenerations, and all degenerations and non-degenerations were formally verified in the proof assistant Lean~4. The graph of primary degenerations of $4$-dimensional Jordan algebras has $73$ vertices and $160$ edges. The variety of $5$-dimensional nilpotent Jordan algebras is stratified into $63$ normal forms, five of which are one- or two-parameter families; together with two special members of a family this gives $65$ objects, and the graph of primary degenerations has $154$ edges. In particular, we describe all irreducible components of the corresponding varieties: the variety of $4$-dimensional Jordan algebras has $10$ irreducible components, and the variety of $5$-dimensional nilpotent Jordan algebras has dimension $22$ and $5$ irreducible components.

entry.title: OmniSpace: Efficient Geometry Awareness for Autonomous Vehicles MLLMs
entry.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable performance on 2D visual tasks, yet enhancing their spatial intelligence for real-world applications such as Autonomous Vehicles (AV) remains an open challenge. Existing geometry-aware MLLMs typically rely on auxiliary 3D models at inference time, introducing pipeline complexity and the risk of cascading failures. In this paper, we present OmniSpace, a simple yet effective plug-and-play paradigm for geometry-aware spatial reasoning from purely 2D observations. Motivated by our finding that current MLLMs are bottlenecked by weak cross-view correspondence and depth estimation, OmniSpace introduces a Camera Pose Injector, a Multi-view Epipolar Attention module, and a 3D Geometric Distillation objective that jointly address these two limitations by transferring geometric knowledge into the model. Extensive experiments show that OmniSpace surpasses existing methods on planning benchmarks (nuScenes, Bench2Drive), risk detection (nuInstruct), language (Omnidrive), and generalization (DriveBench).

entry.title: Relative Langlands duality for linear periods
entry.summary: We prove relative Langlands duality for $X = GL_{p+q}/(GL_p \times GL_q)$. These symmetric spaces arise in the setting of the linear period of Friedberg-Jacquet when $p=q$, and exhibit non-tempered behavior when $q>p+1$. Via the real-symmetric correspondence, we establish a derived Satake equivalence for the real group $G_{\mathbb R}=U(p,q)$, and use it to obtain a constructible realization of coherent sheaves on Kato's exotic nilpotent cones. Along the way, we describe the dual variety of $X$ in terms of the Whittaker cotangent bundle and regular centralizers, viewed as Coulomb branches.

entry.title: Learning to Be Monitored: Causal Bounds and Intervention-Aware Post-Training Recipes for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
entry.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring aims to detect potentially harmful behaviors in large language models (LLMs) from their CoTs. Intervention-based evaluations measure this property by asking whether a monitor can detect the role of an intervention from the CoT when the targeted behavior occurs, typically using minimal-criterion sensitivity ($\mathsf{TPR_{mc}}$) proposed by~\citep{guan2025monitoring}. However, a target behavior observed under intervention is not necessarily caused by it, and we show that this metric can overestimate how often a monitor detects target behaviors actually caused by the intervention. Specifically, we establish $\mathsf{TPR_{mc}}$ as an upper bound on this causal detection rate and derive a complementary lower bound, which provides a tighter evaluation framework for CoT monitorability. With this framework, we study whether LLMs can be trained to make their CoTs easier to monitor. We first construct a training dataset of paired control--intervention tasks spanning multiple intervention types. Using the dataset, we design and apply three intervention-specific training methods based on off-policy self-distillation, reinforcement learning, and on-policy self-distillation to train separate variants of each base model. Across various model-monitor configurations, all three methods generally improve CoT monitorability over the corresponding base models under our extended evaluation framework. Our code is available at https://github.com/xinyue-lxy/learning-to-be-monitored.

entry.title: A Decision Procedure for Probabilistic Kleene Algebra with Angelic Nondeterminism
entry.summary: In Ong et al.~(2025), a new finite automaton model with probabilistic and nondeterministic transitions was introduced, along with a corresponding regular expression language. The key difference from previous approaches is that nondeterminism is formalized in terms of multisets instead of powersets. Automata and expressions are interpreted over the space of probability distributions over multisets of strings with finite multiplicities. The main result of that paper was a full Kleene theorem showing that the two formalisms are equally expressive. In this paper we give a decision procedure for the semantic equivalence of two automata or expressions. The algorithm is based on polyomial algebra and makes use of Gröbner basis techniques for ideal membership testing.

entry.title: Haptic bilateral teleoperation system for free-hand dental procedures
entry.summary: Free-hand dental procedures are typically repetitive, time-consuming and require high precision and manual dexterity. Robots can play a key role in improving procedural accuracy and safety, enhancing patient comfort, and reducing operator workload. However, robotic solutions for free-hand procedures remain limited or completely lacking. To address this gap, we develop a haptic bilateral teleoperation system (HBTS) for free-hand dental procedures (FH-HBTS). The system includes a mechanical end-effector, compatible with standard clinical tools, and equipped with an endoscopic camera for improved visibility of the intervention site. By ensuring motion and force correspondence between the operator's and the robot's actions, monitored through visual feedback, we enhance the operator's sensory awareness and motor accuracy. Furthermore, to ensure procedural safety, we limit interaction forces by scaling the motion references provided to the admittance controller based solely on measured contact forces. This ensures effective force limitation in all contact states without requiring prior knowledge of the environment. The proposed FH-HBTS is validated through a technical evaluation and an in-vitro pre-clinical study conducted on a dental model under clinically representative, yet simplified, conditions. The results show that the system improves the naturalness, safety, and accuracy of teleoperation, highlighting its potential to enhance free-hand dental procedures.

entry.title: Parallel Trends as a Spectrum
entry.summary: Difference-in-differences (DiD) designs are typically used to identify and estimate average causal effects, even though treatment can affect the entire outcome distribution. This has led to a growing interest in distributional DiD methods. However, identifying the full counterfactual distribution requires a parallel trends assumption on the entire distributional dynamics, which can be too strong in practice. We address this problem by introducing a spectrum of identifying restrictions that lie between the average and fully distributional DiD by imposing parallel trends on $L$-moments. This corresponds to a basis expansion of the distributional dynamics. Importantly, each $L$-moment is interpretable as familiar distributional components: location, dispersion, skewness, kurtosis, etc. Researchers can pick and choose which features they want to target. For example, the second $L$-moment identifies the Gini mean difference, but does not require imposing mean-level or higher-order parallel trends. Taking a collection of $L$-moments can approximate distributional dynamics under weaker conditions since it leaves untargeted components unrestricted. We develop conditions under which higher-order $L$-moments decay, efficient estimators, and simultaneous inference across growing collections of moments. We demonstrate the benefits of our framework by exploring distributional changes to healthcare spending after the rollout of Medicare Part D.

entry.title: Coefficient Positivity for Arborescence Ratios of Covering Digraphs
entry.summary: For a directed graph with a chosen root, the arborescence polynomial sums the products of edge weights over all spanning trees directed toward that root. In a finite graph cover, each lifted edge inherits the variable of its base edge. At corresponding roots, the ratio of the cover's arborescence polynomial to the base polynomial is known to be an integer polynomial. We prove that every coefficient of this ratio is nonnegative, resolving the positivity conjecture of Pylyavskyy. The key to the proof is to allow fibers of unequal size and replace the permutations defining a cover by arbitrary maps. For these more general systems, we prove a stronger coefficient-positivity theorem for a determinant derived from the graph Laplacian. The enlarged class is closed under two reductions: contraction of an edge over a base loop and elimination of a base vertex. Both yield nonnegative recurrences for the relevant coefficients in terms of smaller systems, allowing an inductive proof. We also pose the problem of finding a direct combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients.

entry.title: FRB 20210601A: Extreme Temporal Clustering in a Repeating Fast Radio Burst Source as Evidence for a Hidden Class of Episodic Repeaters
entry.summary: Population studies of fast radio burst (FRB) repetition typically model sources using a single distribution of steady, time-averaged burst rates, yet individual sources show significant departures from this assumption. Here we present FRB 20210601A, a source discovered by the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment FRB project (CHIME/FRB) that represents the most extreme such departure yet identified. The source produced at least nine bursts within a single 106.5 s interval -- the highest instantaneous burst rate yet reported from a repeating FRB source at $\gtrsim 2$ Jy ms fluences -- yet remained otherwise undetected despite $\sim 320$ hr of exposure spanning 7 yr. The active interval occurred while the source was in a side-lobe of the CHIME/FRB digitized beams, implying an instantaneous burst rate $\gtrsim2.3\times$ higher ($\gtrsim$ 21 bursts) at main-lobe sensitivity. The source's intense, brief burst storm flanked by apparent quiescence despite substantial exposure is unique among the CHIME/FRB repeater sample, although its burst morphology, excess dispersion measure ($\rm{DM_{excess}} \sim 360$ pc cm$^{-3}$), Faraday rotation measure ($|\rm{RM_{excess}}| \sim 150-170$ rad m$^{-2}$), and temporal scattering ($τ\lesssim 0.37$ ms at 600 MHz) are otherwise typical. Modeling a population of episodically active repeaters (i.e., short burst storms separated by long recurrence times) and accounting for declination-dependent exposure, we forecast $\sim1-4$ additional source discoveries similar to FRB 20210601A over the next decade of CHIME/FRB operations, corresponding to a CHIME/FRB-detectable population of $9^{+200}_{-8}$ sources (68% credible interval). These results demonstrate that highly episodic repeaters could constitute a selection-biased but detectable component of the FRB population, possibly reflecting distinct magnetospheric states or triggering mechanisms.

entry.title: Approaching I/O-optimality for Approximate Attention
entry.summary: We revisit the I/O complexity of attention in large language models. Given query-key-value matrices $Q,K,V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, and a machine with fast memory size $M$, the goal is to compute the "attention matrix" $A=\text{softmax}(Q K ^{\top}/\sqrt{d}) V$ with the minimal number of data transfers between fast and slow memory. Existing methods in the literature, most notably FlashAttention and its variants, incur an I/O cost that depends quadratically on the context length $n$, while a trivial lower bound only requires $Ω(nd)$ I/O's to read the inputs and write the output. In this work we show that the dependence on $n$ can be reduced to almost-linear, by developing I/O-efficient algorithms inspired by the recent approximate attention method of Alman and Song [NeurIPS'23]. We also provide (algorithm-specific) lower bounds in different parameter regimes, which nearly match the corresponding upper bounds, indicating that the proposed algorithms are indeed close to I/O-optimal.
